item.title: GDPR, Sensitive Data and CRM Profiles
item.lead: The CRM section of the dossier directly links privacy law and psychological profiling.

blocks.text: The source states that information about sexual behavior, health, trauma, financial problems, or relationship breakdowns can be stored in CRM dossiers and used for commercial influence. Precisely because such information is potentially sensitive, the legal question, according to the dossier, becomes more significant as the data collection deviates further from the core function of the service.

A legal analysis should not only consider the fact that data is stored, but also the legal basis, purpose, proportionality, retention period, access, processing chain, and international transfer. The source specifically highlights the tension between the commercial function of a CRM and the sensitivity of the data included.

A second question concerns responsibility within the chain. Who is the data controller? Who is the data processor? What access do chat operators have? Where are backups stored? Which entity can be held accountable if a dossier is leaked? These are concretely answerable questions.
The dossier therefore uses the GDPR not only as a protective right, but also as a route to evidence. A thorough privacy investigation can simultaneously reveal an organizational structure.
